newsitem.title: USA: Eli Lilly comfortable with '96 estimates.
newsitem.headline: Eli Lilly comfortable with '96 estimates.

text.p: Eli Lilly & Co Chief Financial Officer and Executive Vice President Charles Golden said Wednesday the company was "reasonably comfortable" with Wall Street's 1996 estimates of $2.63 to $2.67 a share.
The Indianapolis-based pharmaceutical concern reported a profit from continuing operations last year of $2.30 a share.
Golden, speaking to investors at a Montgomery Securities conference here, said Lilly is aiming to not only maintain the market share of its Prozac anti-depressant drug but to increase it.
"We're working very hard not just to sustain Prozac sales but to accelerate them," he told investors.

Golden said the worldwide anti-depressant market is estimated to grow at a 12 to 13 percent rate annually and added "our goal with Prozac is at a minimum to maintain our market share and at a maximum to grow it."

He said through August of this year Prozac sales in the United States have exceeded those of its nearest competitor by 25 percent and he added the company is working for approval of additional indications for the drug.

Analysts see Lilly as the leader in the world wide anti-depressant therapeutic category. Through July, analysts estimate the company held an 18 percent share of the competitive serotonin anti-depressant market.
But analysts also note that with Prozac accounting for more than 30 percent of sales, the company is expected to be under pressure in early 2001 when the patent on the drug is due to expire.

Golden said the company has been working to improve expense and cost controls and is working to decrease its global procurement costs by some eight to nine percent as part of an effort to save some $190 million at the end of the multi-year program.
He also said the company expects to curb growth in costs related to sales, general and administration expenses next year.
